parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, police targeting, facility/bathroom ban, custody rule, or violence against trans people is documented; same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 1996. Against that, there is no documented social acceptance or working visitor-facing protection for gender identity: anti-discrimination protections are framed around sexual orientation, authorities rejected all 8 marker-change requests with no plans to revise citing societal values, and gay culture is described as largely invisible. The absence of domestic gender recognition is resident-facing and not deducted as a visitor exposure, but the documented frontier document-disagreement is an open border question. In a thin dossier, silence is not safety, and conservative institutional signals extrapolate to friction and thin recourse if outed, without reaching universal exposure or organised targeting.
